bib.title: UPRISE: Universal Prompt Retrieval for Improving Zero-Shot Evaluation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: UPRISE: Universal Prompt Retrieval for Improving Zero-Shot Evaluation. Daixuan Cheng, Shaohan Huang, Junyu Bi, Yuefeng Zhan, Jianfeng Liu, Yujing Wang, Hao Sun, Furu Wei, Denvy Deng, Qi Zhang (Microsoft). arXiv:2303.08518v4, 16 Dec 2023 (EMNLP 2023 version; the PDF itself says only "arXiv ... [cs.CL]", so treat the venue as unconfirmed by the text). File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/01-prompt-engineering/sources/cheng-2023-uprise.pdf

COVERAGE: 20 of 20 pages read; 68073 of 68073 chars. All main text, Tables 1-11, limitations and appendices A-F were read. The references were skimmed. Figures 4, 6, 7, 8 and 10 are plots whose values did not extract (Fig. 10 numbers did extract). Note: the target note has no mention of UPRISE or arXiv 2303.08518 in its sources (grep found none), so this is a new citation.

WHAT IT IS (for the note)
UPRISE does not rewrite a prompt. It trains a retriever that picks demonstrations from a pool and prepends them to each zero-shot input. The retriever is tuned with a frozen small LLM as the labeler. So it is "prompt optimization by retrieval", a per-input prompt chosen from a fixed pool.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Method: the frozen LLM's task score labels prompts as positive or negative, and those labels train a bi-encoder retriever with a contrastive loss.
   number: L=50 sampled candidates, B=20 negatives, K=3 retrieved at inference, BERT-base encoders, 3 epochs
   setup: GPT-Neo-2.7B labels; up to 10k examples per task; about 180k pool examples per test cluster; greedy decoding
   quote: "We set the size of the randomly sampled subset to L = 50and the number of (hard) negatives to B = 20." and "we set the번 number K of concatenated prompts to a relatively small value of 3" (verbatim text: "we set the number K of concatenated prompts to a relatively small value of 3, to balance between prompting performance and inference efficiency")
   where: Sec 4, p.4
2. Cross-task gains on GPT-Neo-2.7B (the tuning model), on held-out task clusters. Reading Comprehension average rises from 31.6 to 40.1, and Paraphrase from 47.0 to 61.6.
   number: +8.5 and +14.6 absolute
   setup: 0-shot vs UPRISE, retriever trained on the remaining clusters only (Table 1)
   quote: "we achieve absolute gains of 8.5% and 14.6% in Reading Comprehension and Paraphrase Detection tasks, respectively."
   where: Sec 5.1, p.5
3. Cross-model transfer. The retriever tuned with GPT-Neo-2.7B was applied unchanged to larger models. Cluster averages from Table 1 (0-shot to UPRISE):
   - Reading Comp: BLOOM-7.1B 32.3 to 33.5, OPT-66B 34.6 to 36.2, Davinci 35.5 to 36.8, Davinci-001 45.9 to 53.6
   - Closed-book QA: BLOOM-7.1B 22.0 to 24.2, OPT-66B 23.9 to 27.2, Davinci 26.2 to 29.8, Davinci-001 34.1 to 37.9
   - Paraphrase: BLOOM-7.1B 51.2 to 62.3, OPT-66B 50.7 to 60.6, Davinci 52.9 to 59.7, Davinci-001 47.3 to 59.0
   quote: "Closed-book QA 19.2 23.3 22.0 24.2 23.9 27.2 26.2 29.8 34.1 37.9" (the row is GPT-Neo 19.2/23.3, BLOOM 22.0/24.2, OPT 23.9/27.2, Davinci 26.2/29.8, Davinci-001 34.1/37.9)
   where: Table 1, p.5
4. Gains are not universal. Commonsense and Coreference averages fall or stay flat. Coreference: GPT-Neo 64.0 to 62.1, OPT-66B 73.1 to 68.0, Davinci 70.4 to 68.0, Davinci-001 69.8 to 66.3. NLI falls on text-davinci-001 (50.2 to 46.9), which the authors attribute to that model having been instruction-tuned on such tasks. Sentiment on GPT-Neo falls (62.7 to 61.8).
   quote: "Coreference Resolution 64.0 62.1 69.4 67.0 73.1 68.0 70.4 68.0 69.8 66.3" and "UPRISE has negative impacts on Commonsense Reasoning and Coreference Resolution tasks."
   where: Table 1, Sec 5.1, App D
   Reason given: even few-shot underperforms zero-shot on coreference (59.3 vs 50.6, Table 6). Commonsense is hurt by a format mismatch, since Closed-book QA is the most retrieved type but is a different format.
5. ChatGPT hallucination (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, temperature 0). Fact-checking improves, TruthfulQA does not.
   number: FEVER2.0 51.0 to 56.0; Covid-19 47.0 to 83.0; TruthfulQA 86.3 to 86.3
   setup: human-judged samples of 66 (TruthfulQA), 100 (FEVER2.0) and 100 (Covid-19 scientific subset). The retriever was trained on all listed task types. On Covid-19 the baseline's ambiguous answers were counted wrong.
   quote: "0-SHOT 86.3 51.0 47.0 / UPRISE 86.3 56.0 83.0" and "we observe vanilla zero-shot prompting often leads to ambiguous answers, which we consider the answer incorrect."
   where: Table 2, p.5; App C
   Caveat for the note: small samples, and the Covid-19 jump partly reflects the scoring rule.
6. The retriever must be learned. Random, BM25 and SBERT top-k (KATE style) retrieval all do worse than UPRISE on GPT-Neo-2.7B.
   number: none stated in text (Fig. 6 is a plot)
   quote: "This suggests that word-level (TOPK-BM25) or sentence-level (TOPK-BERT) similarity to the testing input is not the only decisive factor for a good prompt."
   where: Sec 7.1
7. Pool matters. A pool of demonstrations from other tasks beats a pool of raw pre-training text (wikitext-103) on every cluster. Averages, RAW TEXT vs UPRISE: Read 32.0 vs 40.1, Closed 19.3 vs 23.4, Para 44.7 vs 61.6, NLI 37.5 vs 43.0, Senti 60.3 vs 61.8.
   quote: "RAW TEXT 32.0 19.3 44.7 37.5 60.3 / UPRISE 40.1 23.4 61.6 43.0 61.8"
   where: Table 3, p.6
8. Training-task diversity matters. Halving the trained task types lowers performance, but it still beats 0-shot on most types. Training on a single task type generalizes unevenly: Reading Comp and Closed-book QA transfer best.
   number: 50% of types (no figure values in text)
   quote: "The results in Figure 7 do indicate a decline in performance as diversity decreases. Nonetheless, the retriever trained on 50% remaining task types continues to demonstrate better performance than 0-SHOT across most task types."
   where: Sec 8
9. Versus few-shot (Table 4, 3 demos). Zero-shot UPRISE (retriever and pool both from other tasks) is close to or above random few-shot drawn from the target task. UPRISE vs FEW-SHOT: Read 40.1 vs 37.4, Closed 23.3 vs 25.1, Para 61.6 vs 59.1, NLI 43.0 vs 43.4, Senti 61.8 vs 72.7. The retriever trained on all task types, with the target-task pool, is much better: NLI 72.4, Sentiment 82.9, Paraphrase 73.4.
   quote: "UPRISE approaches and even outperforms vanilla few-shot prompting on most task types"
   where: Table 4, Sec 9
   Caveat: sentiment is a clear loss (61.8 vs 72.7), so "most" glosses over that.
10. Cost of training the retriever: 36 hours on 8 V100-32GB GPUs, batch size 2 per GPU, max length 256, LR 1e-5. The filtering step retries up to 7 sampling rounds, which finds a positive for about 90% of examples.
   quote: "Computing Infrastructure 8 V100-32GB GPUs ... Run-time 36 Hours"
   where: Table 5, App B. The "90%" text is in Sec 4: "we found that this is sufficient to identify a positive prompt for 90% of the training examples."
11. What gets retrieved: top-1 retrievals share question type, topic, format or logical relation with the input (Tables 7-11). Cluster-level retrieval ratios are in Fig. 10, e.g. Closed-book QA draws 80.7% of its retrievals from Reading Comprehension, and Paraphrase draws 74.4% from NLI. (The row/column labels in the extraction are scrambled, so check the figure image before quoting a specific pairing.) Paper's text: "high retrieved ratios (e.g., 80.7% for Close-QA and 36.1% for NLI)".
   where: App F

LIMITS
- Authors concede (Limitations): "limited impacts on tasks that are directly formulated as language modeling, such as Coreference Resolution and Commonsense Reasoning". Only language has been tested. Tool-use and multimodal prompts are left to future work. Chain-of-thought demonstrations were not tried.
- Not shown: any comparison with hand-written prompts or with APE-style instruction search; no cost-per-query figure; no confidence intervals or seeds (single run per cell); the evaluated models are 2020-2022 base models, with only ChatGPT as a chat model. The ChatGPT test uses human judging on 66 to 100 samples.
- "Zero-shot" here means no test-task demonstrations. It still prepends 3 demonstrations from other tasks, so it is not the same as zero-shot prompting without any retrieval. This matters for the note's framing.
- Dated: the models (GPT-Neo-2.7B, BLOOM, OPT, davinci, text-davinci-001, gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) are old. Absolute numbers will not carry over to current models.
- The method is fixed to a pool of demonstrations. It selects among existing text and does not generate new instructions.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Rubin et al., 2022, "Learning to retrieve prompts for in-context learning" (EPR): the LLM labels prompts and a retriever is trained on them. Ye et al., 2023 (CEIL) is related work.
- Brown et al., 2020 (in-context learning, multiple-choice scoring); Wei et al., 2022a (FLAN templates, hold-out cluster protocol); Karpukhin et al., 2020 (bi-encoder); van den Oord et al., 2018 (InfoNCE); Liu et al., 2022 (KATE); Devlin et al., 2019 (BERT).
- Contrasted with prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021; Li and Liang, 2021; Liu et al., 2021) and prompt design (Wei et al., 2022b).

CODE: none in the paper. Formulas worth keeping:
- Eq. 1-2: "P + = R(x, P)" then the frozen LLM predicts from "P + ⊕ x".
- Eq. 4 (multiple-choice score): "score (pj, xi) = acc(yi, ypji) · LH(oyi) / Σ_m LH(om)" (accuracy times the normalised gold-option likelihood, to give finer-grained labels than 0/1).
- Eq. 5: InfoNCE loss over 1 positive and 2B negatives.
- Repo: https://github.com/microsoft/LMOps

FIGURES (captions as printed)
- Fig 1, p.1: "UPRISE tunes a prompt retriever on multiple tasks with a small LLM, but conducts inference on unseen task types with a different larger LLM." Shows the cross-task and cross-model idea at a glance.
- Fig 2, p.2: "Typical prompt engineering methods and prompt retrieval." Places prompt design, soft-prompt tuning and prompt retrieval side by side. Best candidate for the note, since it shows where retrieval sits among the optimization methods.
- Fig 3, p.4: "Training and inference pipeline." Shows the frozen-LLM-labels-the-retriever loop. It is the main method diagram and the best candidate if only one figure is used.
- Fig 4, p.5: cross-model average gains of the cross-task retriever (bar plot).
- Fig 5, p.5-6: the Sonny & Cher case where 0-shot gives the wrong answer and UPRISE gives the right one.
- Fig 6, 7, 8, 10: retriever ablation, diversity, single-task generalizability and retrieved-cluster matrix.
Use "scripts/papers/figures.py captions" if the images are needed. I did not run it.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean text, with some words run together inside figure text. In claim 1, my first quote attempt contained a stray token from my own typing; the verbatim string to use is the second form given there ("we set the number K ... efficiency"). Table 1 and Fig. 10 cell alignment came from extraction order, so check them against the page image before publishing any single cell.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- The venue (EMNLP 2023) is not printed in the PDF text, so I did not state it as read.
